To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two new bis(aminoethylenethiol) ligands containing an aminomethyl group in the side chain were prepared.
the new BAT ligands, TMPDA and DEA, have been prepared and complexed with 9 9mTc to give the target complexes, [99mT c]DEA and 99mT c[TMPDA].
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new [99mT c]BAT brain perfusion imaging agent for SPECT.
the development of new technetium- 99m BAT complexes for use as potential agents for the evaluation of brain perfusion with SPECT.

the synthesis and characterization of a series of new technetium-9 9m complexes of the bis (aminoethylthiol) type, and the evaluation of these complexes as brain perfusion imaging probes for use with single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
[99mTcc]DEA-antl is an excellent candidate for the evaluation of cerebral perfusion with SPECT.
[99mTcc]DEA-syri is a promising agent for brain imaging.
[99mTcc]DEA-sym is a potential SPECT brain perfusion imaging agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[99mTec]DEA-sym, with its favorable brain uptake and washout properties and high gray/white matter contrast, is a potential agent for the assessment of regional cerebral perfusin with SPECT.
[99mTC]DEA-synthesis is a promising agent for brain perfusion SPECT imaging.
the syn isomer of [99mTC]DEA appears to be the best of the BAT complexes for brain perfusion imaging with SPECT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the syn isomer of DEA is a better candidate for brain perfusion imaging than TMPDA and that the anti isomer of DEA should not be considered for this purpose.
the DEA ligand is a promising candidate for the development of a brain perfusion imaging agent for single photon emission computed Tomography.

the DEA ligand, with its two amines in a sidechain, has the ability to localize in the brain, whereas, the TMPDA ligand, with a primary amine in the sidechain and a secondary amine in the backbone, does not.
